with $D_0$ acting diagonally, through $D_0/I_0$ on $\bar F_\infty$. Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:integrate-t} gives $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K_0)\cong i_{0*}\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-1)$. The nearby cycles of this sheaf at $0$ vanish, and its stalk at $0$ is $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-1)$; so $R\Phi_0(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K_0))\cong\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-1)[1]$, and $R\Phi(\mathcal J(K_0))_\infty\cong\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-1)$ by~\eqref{eq:localization}. Applying~\eqref{eq:localization} to $K=P$, we obtain $R\Phi_0(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P))\cong\bar F_\infty(-1)[1]$, as required. In the language of Laumon's local Fourier transform $\mathcal F^{(\infty,0')}$, this is the isomorphism $R^{-1}\Phi_0(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(P))\cong\mathcal F^{(\infty,0')}\big(F(\infty)\big)$ of \cite[Prop.~(2.3.2.1)(iii) and D\'ef.~(2.4.2.3)]{Laumon}, together with the formula $\mathcal F^{(\infty,0')}(V)\cong V(-1)$ for unramified $V$; cf.~\cite[Lemma~11]{Katz-Bourbaki}. These references are not used in the argument above.

\emph{The stalk at infinity.} If $n\ge3$, the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:R-global} gives $\bar F=a^*\mathcal G_{n-1}(1)$ with $a(\infty)=c$, so $\bar F_\infty$ is the stalk of $\mathcal G_{n-1}(1)$ at $c$, which is $H^{n-2}_c(Y_c\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f'))$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:lisse}(iii) for $n-1$ variables. If $n=2$, then $\bar F=\mathcal{L}_\psi(-c_2v/(\lambda v+1))$, whose stalk at $\infty$ is the line on which $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ acts by $\psi_q(-c_2/\lambda)$, that is, $H^0_c(Y_c\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f'))$. In both cases $\bar F_\infty$ has dimension $2^{n-1}-1$, and the determinant of $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ on it is $D_{n-1}(c)$. Now $\phi$ acts on $\mathcal G_0$ as $\operatorname{Frob}_q$, with determinant $D_{n-1}(c)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:FT-zero}(i),(iii), and on $\bar F_\infty(-1)$ as $q\operatorname{Frob}_q$, with determinant $q^{2^{n-1}-1}D_{n-1}(c)$. The exact sequence~\eqref{eq:vanishing-zero} gives the formula for $\det(\phi\mid\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0})$. As $I_0$ acts trivially on both outer terms of~\eqref{eq:vanishing-zero}, it acts unipotently on $\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0}$; two choices of $\phi$ differ by an element of $I_0$, which has determinant $1$ there.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:alpha}
For every $n\ge1$, every power $q$ of $p$ and every $h\in(\mathbb{F}_q^\times)^n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:det-fibre}
\det\big(\operatorname{Frob}_q\mid H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))\big)=q^{(n-2)2^{n-1}+1}\,\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big),
\end{equation}
where $Y_h=\{u\in\mathbb{G}_m^n:\langle h,u\rangle=-\lambda\}$ and $f=\sum_iu_i^{-1}$. If $n\ge2$, the constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:det} is $\alpha=p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$; equivalently, for every $h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)$,
\[
\det\big(\operatorname{Frob}_h\mid\mathcal W_n\big)=q^{(n+1)r(n)/2}\,\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big),
\]
and the product of the $r(n)$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$ of $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ on $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$ is $q^{(n-1)r(n)/2}\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big)$. In particular Theorem~\ref{thmE}(i) holds.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
We argue by induction on $n$. For $n=1$, $Y_h$ is the point $u_1=-\lambda/h_1$, at which $f=-h_1/\lambda$; so $H^0_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$ is a line on which $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ acts by $\psi_q(-h_1/\lambda)$, and~\eqref{eq:det-fibre} holds because $e(1)=0$. Let $n\ge2$, and assume~\eqref{eq:det-fibre} for $n-1$ variables.

\emph{Step 1: a second computation of $\det(\phi\mid\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0})$.} Let $q=p^k$, let $c\in(\mathbb{F}_q^\times)^{n-1}$, and let $D_0$, $I_0$ and $\phi$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:vanishing-zero}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:FT-zero}(iii), $\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0}$ is the generic stalk of $\mathcal G_n|_{C_c}(1)$, as a representation of $D_0$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:lisse}(iv),(vi), the generic stalk of $\mathcal G_n|_{C_c}$ has a $D_0$-stable filtration whose graded pieces are the generic stalk of $\mathcal W_n|_{C_c}$ and the spaces $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-j)^{\oplus m_{n,j}}$, $1\le j\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, on which $\phi$ acts as multiplication by $q^j$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:det}, $\det(\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})\cong\mathcal{L}_\psi(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}h_1)\otimes\mathcal E$, where $\mathcal E$ is the geometrically constant sheaf on $C_c$ on which $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ acts by $\alpha^k\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(c_2+\cdots+c_n)\big)$. Both factors extend to lisse sheaves on $\mathbb A^1_{h_1}$. So $I_0$ acts trivially on the determinant of the generic stalk of $\mathcal W_n|_{C_c}$, and $\phi$ acts on it by the Frobenius at $0$ of the extension, that is, by $\psi_q(0)\,\alpha^k\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(c_2+\cdots+c_n)\big)$. As $\mathcal G_n|_{C_c}$ has rank $2^n-1$, we have $\det(\phi\mid\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0})=q^{-(2^n-1)}\det\big(\phi\mid(\mathcal G_n|_{C_c})_{\bar\eta_0}\big)$, and therefore
\[
\det\big(\phi\mid\mathcal G_{\bar\eta_0}\big)=q^{S_1(n)-(2^n-1)}\,\alpha^k\,\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(c_2+\cdots+c_n)\big).
\]

\emph{Step 2: the value of $\alpha$.} By the induction hypothesis, applied to $c$, $D_{n-1}(c)=q^{e(n-1)}\psi_q\big(-2^{n-2}\lambda^{-1}(c_2+\cdots+c_n)\big)$, so that $D_{n-1}(c)^2=q^{2e(n-1)}\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(c_2+\cdots+c_n)\big)$. Comparing Step~1 with Lemma~\ref{lem:vanishing-zero}, the values of $\psi_q$ cancel, and Lemma~\ref{lem:numerology}(ii),(iii) gives
\[
\alpha^k=q^{2e(n-1)+2^{n-1}-1+2^n-1-S_1(n)}=q^{e(n)+2^n-1-S_1(n)}=q^{(n+1)r(n)/2}.
\]
For $q=p$ this is $\alpha=p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$.

\emph{Step 3: every $h$.} Let $h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)$. Theorem~\ref{thm:det} and Step~2 give the formula for $\det(\operatorname{Frob}_h\mid\mathcal W_n)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:lisse}(iii),(iv),(vi), the stalk of $\mathcal G_n$ at $\bar h$ is $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))(-1)$, of dimension $2^n-1$, and it has a $\operatorname{Frob}_h$-stable filtration with graded pieces $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(-j)^{\oplus m_{n,j}}$ and $(\mathcal W_n)_{\bar h}$. Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\det\big(\operatorname{Frob}_q\mid H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))\big)&=q^{S_1(n)-(2^n-1)}\det(\operatorname{Frob}_h\mid\mathcal W_n)\\
&=q^{e(n)}\,\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big)
\end{aligned}
\]
by Lemma~\ref{lem:numerology}(iii), which is~\eqref{eq:det-fibre}. Finally, by Theorem~\ref{thm:fibre}(iv) and Theorem~\ref{thm:lisse}(iv), the eigenvalues of weight $n-1$ on $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$ are the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Frob}_h$ on $(\mathcal W_n)_{\bar h}$ divided by $q$, so their product is $q^{-r(n)}\det(\operatorname{Frob}_h\mid\mathcal W_n)$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:det-all-h}
Let $h\in\mathbb{F}_q^n$ have exactly $a\ge1$ nonzero coordinates. Then
\[
\det\big(\operatorname{Frob}_q\mid H^{n-1}_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))\big)=q^{(a-2)2^{a-1}+1}\,\psi_q\big(-2^{a-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big).
\]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
In the notation of the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:all-h}, $R\Gamma_c(Y_h\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))\cong R\Gamma_c(Y_{h_I}\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f_I))[-(n-a)]$ compatibly with $\operatorname{Frob}_q$, and $\sum_{i\in I}h_i=h_1+\cdots+h_n$. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:alpha} with $n$ replaced by $a$.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:Garith}
Let $n\ge2$, let $\gamma\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ be the element with $\iota_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)=p^{-(n+1)/2}>0$, and let $\mathcal W_n^0=\mathcal W_n\otimes\gamma^{\deg}$, as in the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:M2}. Then $\mathcal W_n^0$ is pure of weight $0$,
\[
\det\mathcal W_n^0\cong\mathcal{L}_\psi(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)),
\]
and the arithmetic monodromy group $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)$, the Zariski closure of the image of $\pi_1(S)$ acting on $V$, is
\[
G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)=G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n)=\big\{g\in\operatorname{GL}(V):\det(g)^p=1\big\}.
\]
In particular Theorem~\ref{thmE}(iii) holds.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Since $\mathcal W_n$ is pure of weight $n+1$ and $|\iota_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)|=p^{-(n+1)/2}$, the sheaf $\mathcal W_n^0$ is pure of weight $0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:numerology}(iii), $\frac12(n+1)r(n)$ is an integer, so $\iota_{\mathbb C}(\gamma^{r(n)})=p^{-(n+1)r(n)/2}$ is a rational number. A field isomorphism is the identity on $\mathbb Q$, hence $\gamma^{r(n)}=p^{-(n+1)r(n)/2}=\alpha^{-1}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:alpha}, and $\det\mathcal W_n^0=\det\mathcal W_n\otimes(\gamma^{r(n)})^{\deg}$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf above, by Theorem~\ref{thm:det}. For a morphism $g\colon S\to\mathbb A^1$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the character of $\pi_1(S)$ defined by $\mathcal{L}_\psi(g)$ is the composite of the homomorphism $\pi_1(S)\to\pi_1(\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb{F}_p})$ induced by $g$ with the character defined by the Artin--Schreier sheaf $\mathcal{L}_\psi(x)$ on $\mathbb A^1_x$. The latter factors through the Galois group $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the Artin--Schreier covering $y\mapsto y^p-y$ of $\mathbb A^1_x$, so it takes values in $\mu_p$. So every element of the image of $\pi_1(S)$ has determinant in $\mu_p$, and so has every element of its Zariski closure: $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)\subseteq\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$. This group is $G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:Ggeom}, and $G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n)=G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n^0)\subseteq G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)$, because $\gamma^{\deg}$ is geometrically constant.

The result does not depend on $\iota_{\mathbb C}$. Another choice of $\iota_{\mathbb C}$ replaces $\gamma$ by $\pm\gamma$. If $n$ is odd, then $\gamma=p^{-(n+1)/2}$ is rational and does not change. If $n$ is even, then $r(n)$ is even, as $\binom n{n/2}$ is, so $-1\in\operatorname{SL}(V)\subseteq G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)$, and replacing $\gamma$ by $-\gamma$ multiplies the image of each Frobenius element by $-1$, which does not change the Zariski closure of the image of $\pi_1(S)$.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:Garith-unnormalized}
Without the normalization, $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n)=\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Indeed $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n)$ contains $G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n)\supseteq\operatorname{SL}(V)$, and its image under $\det$ is a closed subgroup of $\mathbb{G}_m$ that contains $\det(\operatorname{Frob}_{h_0}\mid\mathcal W_n)=p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}\psi\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}n\big)$ for $h_0=(1,\dots,1)\in S(\mathbb{F}_p)$. This element has infinite order, so the image is all of $\mathbb{G}_m$.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:fourth-n2}
Let $n=2$ and fix $p$. As $q\to\infty$ through powers of $p$,
\[
\sum_{h\in\mathbb{F}_q^2}|\Sigma_2(h)|^4=2q^4+O_p\big(q^{7/2}\big).
\]
In particular Theorem~\ref{thmD}(iii) holds.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:monodromy}, $G\supseteq\operatorname{SL}_2$. Under $\operatorname{SL}_2$ the representation $V\otimes V$ is the sum of $\operatorname{Sym}^2V$ and $\bigwedge^2V$, irreducible of dimensions $3$ and $1$, so $\operatorname{End}_G(V\otimes V)\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\operatorname{SL}_2}(V\otimes V)$ has dimension at most $2$. It contains the identity and the symmetry of $V\otimes V$, which come from the morphisms $\mathrm{id}$ and the symmetry of $\mathcal W_2\otimes\mathcal W_2$ defined over $\mathbb{F}_p$. So the geometric invariants of $\mathcal E_4=\mathcal W_2^{\otimes2}\otimes(\mathcal W_2^\vee)^{\otimes2}$ form a space of dimension $2$ on which $\operatorname{Frob}_p$ acts trivially. Moreover $-1\in\operatorname{SL}_2\subseteq G$ acts on $V\otimes V\otimes V^\vee$ by $-1$, so the sheaf $\mathcal E_3=\mathcal W_2^0\otimes\mathcal W_2^0\otimes(\mathcal W_2^0)^\vee$, with $\mathcal W_2^0$ as in the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:M2}, has no geometric invariants. Lemma~\ref{lem:averages} gives
\[
\sum_{h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)}|A^0_q(h)|^4=2q^2+O_p\big(q^{3/2}\big),\qquad\sum_{h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)}|A^0_q(h)|^2A^0_q(h)=O_p\big(q^{3/2}\big).
\]
By~\eqref{eq:normalized}, $\Sigma_2(h)=-(z+1)$ with $z=q^{1/2}A^0_q(h)$, and
\[
|z+1|^4=|z|^4+4|z|^2\operatorname{Re}z+4(\operatorname{Re}z)^2+2|z|^2+4\operatorname{Re}z+1.
\]
Summing over $S(\mathbb{F}_q)$, the first term gives $2q^4+O_p(q^{7/2})$, the second $O_p(q^3)$, and the remaining terms $O(q^3)$, since $|A^0_q(h)|\le2$. The points outside $S(\mathbb{F}_q)$ contribute $O(q)$.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:equidistribution}
Let $n\ge2$, let $r=r(n)$, let $K_n=\{g\in\mathrm U(r):\det(g)^p=1\}$, and let $\gamma$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:Garith}. For $q=p^k$ and $h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)$, the semisimplification of $\gamma^k\operatorname{Frob}_h$ acting on the stalk of $\mathcal W_n$ at $\bar h$ is conjugate, through $\iota_{\mathbb C}$, to an element $\theta_{q,h}$ of $K_n$, well defined up to conjugacy, and
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\theta_{q,h}=A^0_q(h),\qquad\det\theta_{q,h}=\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big).
\]
As $k\to\infty$, the conjugacy classes $\theta_{q,h}$, $h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)$, become equidistributed with respect to the image of the Haar probability measure of $K_n$ on its space of conjugacy classes. In particular Theorem~\ref{thmF} holds.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Garith}, $\mathcal W_n^0$ is a lisse sheaf on the smooth geometrically connected variety $S$, pure of weight $0$, with $G_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathcal W_n^0)=G_{\mathrm{geom}}(\mathcal W_n^0)=G$; its Frobenius at $h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is $\gamma^k\operatorname{Frob}_h$. Through $\iota_{\mathbb C}$, the group $G$ becomes $\{g\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb C):\det(g)^p=1\}$, of which $K_n$ is a maximal compact subgroup. Deligne's equidistribution theorem \cite[Th.~3.5.3]{Deligne}, in the form \cite[Th.~9.2.6]{KatzSarnak} for smooth geometrically connected bases of any dimension, therefore applies to $\mathcal W_n^0$: the classes $\theta_{q,h}$ are defined as stated, and they become equidistributed. Moreover $\operatorname{Tr}\theta_{q,h}=\iota_{\mathbb C}\big(\gamma^kA_q(h)\big)=q^{-(n+1)/2}A_q(h)=A^0_q(h)$, and $\det\theta_{q,h}=\iota_{\mathbb C}\big(\gamma^{kr}\alpha^k\big)\,\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:det}, with $\gamma^r\alpha=1$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:alpha} and the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:Garith}.

For Theorem~\ref{thmF}, let $\varphi$ be a continuous function on the disc $\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le r\}$. Then $g\mapsto\varphi(\operatorname{Tr} g)$ is a continuous central function on $K_n$, so the equidistribution gives
\[
\frac1{(q-1)^n}\sum_{h\in S(\mathbb{F}_q)}\varphi\big(A^0_q(h)\big)\longrightarrow\int_{K_n}\varphi(\operatorname{Tr} g)\,dg\qquad(k\to\infty),
\]
where $A^0_q(h)=q^{-(n-1)/2}\big((-1)^{n-1}\Sigma_n(h)-c_n(q)\big)$ by~\eqref{eq:normalized}. For the absolute values take $\varphi(z)=\varphi_1(|z|)$ with $\varphi_1$ continuous on $[0,r]$. The group $K_n$ is the union of the cosets $z\,\mathrm{SU}(r)$ with $z$ a scalar satisfying $z^{rp}=1$, and $|\operatorname{Tr}(zg)|=|\operatorname{Tr} g|$; so the Haar integral of $\varphi_1(|\operatorname{Tr} g|)$ over $K_n$ equals its Haar integral over $\mathrm{SU}(r)$.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:conductor}
Let $n\ge2$, $c\in(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p^\times)^{n-1}$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a subquotient of $(\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})^{\otimes a}\otimes\big((\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})^\vee\big)^{\otimes b}$ for some $a,b\ge0$. Then $\operatorname{Swan}_0(\mathcal E)=0$, all breaks of $\mathcal E$ at $\infty$ are at most $1$, and $\operatorname{Swan}_\infty(\mathcal E)\le\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$. In particular, for every irreducible algebraic representation $\varrho$ of $\operatorname{GL}_{r(n)}$, the sheaf $\varrho(\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})$ satisfies $\operatorname{Swan}_0+\operatorname{Swan}_\infty\le\dim\varrho$; for $\varrho=\operatorname{Sym}^k$ the bound is $\binom{k+r(n)-1}{r(n)-1}$.
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Tameness at $0$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:boundary}) passes to duals, tensor products and subquotients. By Theorem~\ref{thm:infinity}(i), the breaks of $\mathcal W_n|_{C_c}$ at $\infty$ are $0$ and $1$, and the dual has the same breaks. By Lemma~\ref{lem:breaks}(i), all breaks of the tensor product are at most $1$, and the breaks of a subquotient are among those of the module. Hence $\operatorname{Swan}_\infty(\mathcal E)\le\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$. Finally, every irreducible algebraic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_r$ is a direct summand of some $\mathrm{St}^{\otimes a}\otimes(\mathrm{St}^\vee)^{\otimes b}$, where $\mathrm{St}$ is the standard representation, and $\operatorname{Sym}^k$ has dimension $\binom{k+r-1}{r-1}$.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
We treated $n=2$ with $p\in\{3,5,7\}$ and $n=3$ with $p\in\{3,5\}$, for several $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^n$. These include $h=(1,1)$, which lies on a divisor $L_\varepsilon=0$. For each such $h$ we computed $\Sigma_n(h)$ over $\mathbb F_{p^m}$ for $1\le m\le2^n$ by~\eqref{eq:intro-factor}, the Kloosterman sums over $\mathbb F_{p^m}$ being computed by a fast Fourier transform on $\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:fibre}(iv), these numbers give the power sums of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Frob}_p$ on $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$. Newton's identities, applied to the first $2^n-1$ of them, determine a polynomial of degree $2^n-1$. Its roots predict the last power sum to within a relative error of $2\cdot10^{-13}$. Their absolute values agree with Theorem~\ref{thmA}, which predicts $r(n)$ roots of absolute value $p^{(n-1)/2}$ and $m_{n,k}$ roots of absolute value $p^{k-1}$, to within a relative error of $2\cdot10^{-7}$. The roots of weight $0$ are equal to $1$, as Theorem~\ref{thmA} asserts, to within $10^{-6}$; for $n=3$ this was checked for all $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^3$ with $p\in\{3,5,7\}$ and $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$. The deviation is of the size expected for a double root computed in double precision.
\item \emph{The lower eigenvalues for $n=4$.} For $p=3$ and the five vectors $h=(1,1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1,2)$, $(1,1,2,2)$, $(1,2,2,2)$ and $(2,2,2,2)$ we subtracted $3+2p^m$, the contribution predicted by Theorem~\ref{thmA} for the eigenvalue $1$ with multiplicity $3$ and the eigenvalue $p$ with multiplicity $2$, from the power sums for $1\le m\le11$. Newton's identities, applied to the first ten differences, give ten roots of absolute value $p^{3/2}$ to within $2\cdot10^{-5}$, and these predict the eleventh difference to within a relative error of $3\cdot10^{-13}$.
\item \emph{Theorems~\ref{thmE}(i) and~\ref{thm:alpha}.} Let $\delta_q(h)$ be the product of the $r(n)$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$ of $\operatorname{Frob}_q$ on $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$, computed from the power sums as in~(a) and~(b). By Theorem~\ref{thm:alpha}, $\delta_q(h)=q^{(n-1)r(n)/2}\psi_q\big(-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)\big)$. We compared $\delta_p(h)$ with this value for all $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^2$ with $p\le13$ and $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$; for all $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^3$ with $p\in\{3,5,7\}$ and $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$; and for $n=4$, $p=3$ and the five vectors $h$ of~(b). In all cases the ratio is $1$ to within $3\cdot10^{-14}$. We also computed the determinant of $\operatorname{Frob}_p$ on the whole of $H^{n-1}_c(Y_h,\mathcal{L}_\psi(f))$, from the first $2^n-1$ power sums by Newton's identities, and compared it with~\eqref{eq:det-fibre}: for all $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^2$ with $p\in\{3,5,7,11,13\}$ and for all $h\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^3$ with $p\in\{3,5,7\}$, with $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$ in each case, the ratio is $1$ to within $4\cdot10^{-13}$.
\item \emph{Theorem~\ref{thmD}(i).} The three identities of Proposition~\ref{prop:low-moments} hold to within a relative error of $10^{-14}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and odd $p\le11$, and for $n=4$ and $p\le7$, with $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$.
\item
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
For $(n,p)\in\{(2,5),(2,7),(3,3),(3,5),(3,7),(4,3)\}$, several $c\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^{n-1}$ and $\lambda\in\{1,2\}$, we computed the traces of Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n|_{C_c}$ over $\mathbb F_{p^m}$ from Theorem~\ref{thmB}, and from them the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Frob}_p$ on $H^1_c(C_c\otimes\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p,\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})$. This group has dimension $2^{n-1}$, by~\eqref{eq:GOS} and Theorem~\ref{thmC}(i),(ii). The invariants at $0$ and at $\infty$, whose Jordan structure is given by Theorem~\ref{thmC}(i),(ii), and \cite[1.8.4 and 3.2.3]{Deligne} predict its weights: $2$ and $4$ for $n=2$; $3,3,4,4$ for $n=3$; and $4$ six times and $6$ twice for $n=4$. These are the weights found, and the computed eigenvalues predict the next power sum to within a relative error of $10^{-13}$. Theorem~\ref{thmC} also predicts the cohomology of a twist. Since $2\ne0$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$, Lemma~\ref{lem:breaks}(ii) shows that after tensoring with $\mathcal{L}_\psi(-h_1/\lambda)(\infty)$ both the tame part and the part of slope $1$ of $(\mathcal W_n|_{C_c})(\infty)$ become isoclinic of slope $1$. By Theorem~\ref{thmC}(i),(ii) and~\eqref{eq:GOS}, the $L$-function of $\mathcal W_n|_{C_c}\otimes\mathcal{L}_\psi(-h_1/\lambda)$ on $C_c$ is therefore a polynomial of degree $r(n)$. For $(n,p,\lambda)\in\{(2,5,2),(2,7,1),(3,3,2),(3,5,1),(4,3,1)\}$, with one vector $c$ in each case, the power sums of its inverse roots, computed as above, satisfy a linear recurrence of order $r(n)$ and of no smaller order.
\item \emph{Theorem~\ref{thmD}(ii).} Let $R_n(p)$ be the ratio of $\sum_{h\in\mathbb{F}_p^n}|\Sigma_n(h)|^4$ to $2p^{3n-2}$.
\begin{itemize}
\item For $n=3$ and the primes $23\le p\le53$, $R_3(p)$ increases from $0.754$ to $0.882$, and $p\,(1-R_3(p))$ stays between $5.6$ and $6.3$.
\item For $n=4$ and $11\le p\le23$, $R_4(p)$ increases from $0.684$ to $0.854$, and $p\,(1-R_4(p))$ stays between $3.3$ and $3.5$.
\end{itemize}
This agrees with Theorem~\ref{thmD}(ii).
\item \emph{The fourth moment, Section~\ref{sec:fourth}.}
\begin{itemize}
\item The formula of Lemma~\ref{lem:diag} holds to within $10^{-10}$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ and all odd primes $p\le31$.
\item For $p\in\{5,7,11,13\}$, the number of points of $\Gamma_t$ was counted directly. The formula of Lemma~\ref{lem:plane} then holds to within $10^{-11}$ for all $t\in(\mathbb{F}_p^\times)^4$, and on $\mathcal T_G$ one finds $|a_t|\le1.81\,p^{1/2}$, as Corollary~\ref{cor:hasse} requires.
\end{itemize}
\item \emph{Section~\ref{sec:polytope} and Remark~\ref{rem:collision}.}
\begin{itemize}
\item For $2\le n\le5$ we decided, by linear programming, which subsets of the vertex set of $P_n$ are vertex sets of faces. The resulting face numbers agree with Proposition~\ref{prop:structure}(iv), and the normalized volume of $\Delta_n$, computed from its convex hull, is $2^n$, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:volume}.
\item Over $\mathbb R$, for $n=2$ and $h=(1,(1+\delta)^2)$ with $\delta=10^{-1},10^{-2},10^{-3}$, the two points given by Proposition~\ref{prop:crit}, namely
\[
\Big(-\frac1{2+\delta},\,-\frac1{(1+\delta)(2+\delta)},\,(2+\delta)^2\Big)\quad\text{and}\quad\Big(\frac1\delta,\,-\frac1{\delta(1+\delta)},\,\delta^2\Big),
\]
satisfy the critical equations up to a residual of $2\cdot10^{-14}$. The second one escapes to infinity as $\delta\to0$, as described in Remark~\ref{rem:collision}.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end head-2 -->
